item.title: South Korea's Base Group Plans $150 Million Lifeline for Foundation
item.description: Seoul-based Base Group is preparing to invest $150 million in Foundation, which has not paid staff since October 30, Reuters reports. The deal would deepen Base's ties to the Trump family, which Democratic senators questioned in August.

item.title: OpenAI Folds Its Robotics Team Into Research as GPT-6 Astra Takes On Robot Control
item.description: Six months after launching OpenAI Robotics, the company has moved its robotics researchers under Mark Chen and its hardware teams under Greg Brockman, saying general models like GPT-6 Astra can run robots directly.

item.title: Apptronik's RL Lead Says Legs, Not Wheels, Make Robots Safe to Work Beside
item.description: Kyle Morgenstein argues the "fits in human spaces" case for humanoids is really about safety: legs keep a robot compliant with small actuators, while wheeled bases carry large reflected inertia.

item.title: NJIT's PHD-Hand Uses Linkages, Not Tendons, in a Humanoid Hand You Can Print for Under $650
item.description: NJIT researchers built PHD-Hand, a 570 g, 3D-printable humanoid hand with 15 linkage-driven joints and a parts cost under $650. The paper is accepted at IEEE Humanoids 2026, and the design will be open-sourced.

item.title: IntelliProve Raises €2.7M to Bring Camera-Based Vital Signs to Humanoid Robots
item.description: The Belgian startup reads heart rate, breathing and blood pressure from a 30-second face scan with an ordinary camera. After building it into virtual-care apps in 50+ countries, it now wants the same software running on humanoid and assistive robots.
